title: Option C Relational Overhaul: Strict 3NF Decomposition, Pure Junction Tables & Multi-Tier Verification
summary_excerpt: Decomposed the polymorphic users table into clean 3NF with Class Table Inheritance, converted applications into a pure junction table with relational hydration, fixed a subtle MySQL left-to-right SET evaluation bug in vacancy auto-closure, enforced concurrency quota ceilings with SELECT FOR UPDATE, and verified 201/201 multi-tier test assertions via Bun and Playwright.
full_story:
September 12 was our most significant data architecture and reliability sprint to date. We committed to Option C: full Third Normal Form (3NF) relational refactoring with Class Table Inheritance, purged all denormalized snapshots, resolved insidious concurrency edge cases in vacancy auto-closure, and certified the entire system across 201 automated test assertions powered by Bun and Playwright.

Our database had historically relied on a wide, polymorphic users table packed with mutually exclusive nullable columns for student program and course records and employer office accreditation. Today, we dismantled that flat design. We decomposed identity into a pure authentication supertype users and two dedicated 1-to-1 subtype profile tables: student_profiles and employer_profiles, sharing primary keys with cascading referential actions. Simultaneously, applications was stripped of duplicated snapshot fields (such as student names, contacts, and job titles), transforming it into a lean, pure 3NF junction table governed by a compound UNIQUE(job_id, student_id) constraint.

Zero-Downtime Backward Compatibility via Hydration

Refactoring core database tables can easily break presentation layers across student, employer, and administrative views. To achieve zero regressions without modifying dozens of front-end templates, we engineered a sophisticated relational hydration layer in includes/data-helper.php. Functions like get_user_base_query(), hydrate_user(), hydrate_job(), and hydrate_application() dynamically execute optimized SQL joins at query time to synthesize all expected attributes on the fly with zero PHP notices or warnings.

Adversarial Auditing: Catching the Left-to-Right SET Bug

During our adversarial stress audit, our test harness uncovered a subtle, critical defect in vacancy auto-closure. In MySQL, UPDATE ... SET clauses are evaluated left to right. Because slots_filled = slots_filled + 1 executed first, the subsequent CASE condition checking slots_filled + 1 >= slots_total was reading the already-incremented value! This resulted in premature auto-closure after only N-1 candidates were accepted. We eliminated the redundant increment in the CASE condition and wrapped applicant acceptance in a pessimistic SELECT ... FOR UPDATE lock to strictly enforce vacancy capacity ceilings against concurrent acceptances.

Fast Multi-Tier Verification with Bun & Playwright

To verify that our refactored relational foundation is rock-solid, we migrated our test runner execution to Bun for sub-second tooling startup. We ran our comprehensive dual integration suite (61/61 passed), the adversarial edge case audit (29/29 passed), the lifecycle notifications suite, and all 8 Playwright browser automation suites across desktop, half-screen (680px-960px), and mobile viewports. The outcome was definitive: 201 out of 201 automated test assertions passed cleanly with zero database constraint violations and zero console errors.

Strict UI Clean UI & Typography Enforcement

We also performed a final pass on UI cleanliness, removing legacy decorative badge pills and eyebrow tags above headings in admin/categories.php, admin/updates.php, and update-detail.php. In strict compliance with our UI guidelines, headings now stand with clean typographic hierarchy, reserving badges strictly for dynamic application workflow states and notification counters.
key_takeaways: Refactored database to strict 3NF with Class Table Inheritance (users, student_profiles, employer_profiles).
Converted applications to a pure 3NF junction table with dynamic SQL hydration and compound uniqueness.
Patched MySQL left-to-right SET evaluation flaw in vacancy auto-closure and added SELECT FOR UPDATE ceiling locks.
Hardened registration role tampering, unscoped selectors, and eliminated decorative pill clutter above headings.
Achieved 100% pass rate across all 201 multi-tier test assertions (111 Playwright + 61 integration + 29 adversarial) via Bun.

title: Sealing Demo Backdoors, Unifying Table Flags & Shipping the Accepted-Student Flow
summary_excerpt: Gated the passwordless demo hooks to loopback-only, fixed an Apply redirect that silently signed guests in as another student, replaced rainbow table pills with a uniform dot-flag system, cut the job-card photo to a single overlay, and shipped an opt-in withdraw-others flow for accepted students — every change proven with curl traces and Playwright screenshots.
full_story:
September 11 was a trust-and-clarity sprint: every path that could silently sign a visitor in as someone else got sealed, tables and cards were stripped of pill clutter, and accepted students finally got a dignified way to release their other pending applications — each change proven with curl traces and Playwright screenshots.

A production audit with fresh eyes surfaced an uncomfortable truth: our beloved demo conveniences had leaked into user-facing flows. The E2E reset and passwordless login hooks in login.php answered to anyone who asked, and worse, the guest Apply redirect pointed at login.php?demo=student — so a visitor who clicked Apply Now on the homepage woke up signed in as Juan Dela Cruz. I gated both hooks to loopback-only plus a non-production APP_ENV with a strict student/employer/admin role whitelist, and rerouted guests to the plain login form carrying a whitelisted next return-to target (relative portal paths only — an evil.com payload was curl-tested and rejected). After a manual sign-in, students land back on the exact requisition they wanted.

Paper Discipline: Pills, Emojis & Phantom Domains

The shared render_page_head() helper defaulted every page title to a green badge pill, in direct violation of our own badges-for-data-only law — it now emits a plain-text kicker, and the homepage and forgot-password pills followed it into eyebrow text. All eight category preset emojis (duplicated across both admin modals) became proper Bootstrap icons, all twelve Campus AI reply templates were de-emojied with the JSON API contract returned to plain text, and six stray campus-hire.edu contacts were unified to the real kld.edu.ph domain. The CAMPUS FAQ badge and its siblings (AI Companion, Student Career Copilot) were purged from both fullscreen chatbot modals and the speech bubble, the redundant green dark-mode switch in Settings was deleted in favor of the segmented control, and the duplicate Back to Vacancies button on job details was removed.

Tables: One Box, One Dot

The analytics table swapped pill classes per cell value, so IN PROGRESS rendered visibly larger than Open Quota and a 1/5 fill count looked nothing like its 0/6 neighbors. The new .cell-flag system gives every state one identical 28px box — ink text, hairline border — with meaning carried only by a 7px status dot (filled, in-progress, over-quota, open), all tokens carrying dark-mode values. Fill counts are now permanently neutral chips since the ratio bar and the flag already tell the story, the decorative Term pill became plain text, and the job-card photo dropped from four overlay pills to a single Featured ribbon with employer type, category, and pay relocated to a clean body metadata row.

Accepted-Student Flow: Prompt, Never Force

No auto-withdraw existed — accepting a student only bumped slot counters and sent a notification. I deliberately chose prompt-to-withdraw over silent auto-withdraw: students may legitimately stack OJT with part-time work, and silent deletes invite RA 10173 disputes and confused supervisors. A CSRF-guarded withdraw_others handler (pending-only, ownership-checked, confirm-guarded) powers a congratulations banner that persists across logins until the record is clean. I staged a demo Juan with one acceptance and two pending applications, captured the screenshots, then deleted the demo rows and reverted — with the database verified byte-identical to its prior state.
key_takeaways: Gated ?reset/?demo hooks to loopback + non-production with role whitelisting, and fixed a guest Apply redirect that auto-logged visitors in as another student.
Shipped a whitelisted next return-to flow so guests land back on their exact requisition after a manual sign-in, with open redirects curl-tested shut.
Replaced per-value table pills with a uniform .cell-flag dot system and cut job-card photos to a single Featured overlay.
Built an opt-in withdraw-others flow for accepted students with CSRF + ownership guards, proven via Playwright screenshots with full demo-data cleanup.

sprint_badge: DAY 13 · DUAL PERSONAS & CYBER GLITCH ENGINE
title: Dual-Persona Developer Photography, Cyber Glitch & RGB Split Transitions, Unified Chatbot Modal & Global Dark Overrides
summary_excerpt: Engineered dynamic dual-persona developer photography with light/dark portraits across all team touchpoints, crafted a 300ms hardware-accelerated Cyber Glitch & RGB Split transition with Hover Peek preview, unified the FAQ Chatbot with the index 3D robot companion modal, and resolved global dark mode contrast anomalies.
full_story:
Today brought our system's visual identity, responsiveness, and interactive polish to an unprecedented level. We engineered dynamic dual-persona developer photography with custom Cyber Glitch and RGB Split transitions, unified our Campus AI assistant modal across pages, and resolved complex dark mode contrast edge cases.

As part of our mission to deliver a world-class institutional experience, our team needed to embody the dual character of our platform: clean, crisp institutional day-to-day operations in daytime mode, and high-performance engineering focus in dark mode. We introduced formal dual-persona 2x2 institutional portraits for all six developers—featuring daytime institutional attire and sleek dark mode photography across the About Us team grid, the DevBlog coverflow, and the floating landing page circles.

Cyber Glitch & RGB Split Transition Engine

Rather than settling for a standard opacity fade when toggling themes, I designed and coded a custom, hardware-accelerated Cyber Glitch & RGB Split Transition. Built using CSS3 drop-shadow chromatic aberration (splitting into cyan #00F0FF and neon crimson #FF1E56 channels), horizontal slice jitter (skewX and subpixel displacements), and an animated scanline sweep, the 320ms transition delivers a tactile, sci-fi cyberpunk feel without any audio intrusion or performance hitching.

To eliminate any perceptual latency or white flicker during rapid toggling, the engine runs an asset preloading cycle on DOM ready, caching both light and dark portraits in browser memory. The image source swap executes at the exact 140ms midpoint peak of maximum jitter distortion, ensuring a seamless visual transformation. Furthermore, I engineered an interactive Hover Peek capability: hovering over any developer card or floating bubble triggers a micro-glitch preview revealing the alternate persona, smoothly restoring when the cursor leaves.

Unified Campus AI Assistant Modal

On faqs.php, the chatbot previously rendered as an isolated offcanvas drawer that conflicted with our paper design language. Today, I completely unified the FAQ chatbot interface with our flagship full-screen 2-column modal from the index page. Powered by our Three.js 3D GLTF robot companion and NVIDIA NIM AI Cloud Gateway, the unified assistant modal delivers full multi-turn conversational intelligence, instant topic suggestions, and zero-reload responsiveness across the portal.

Dark Mode Typography & Contrast Hardening

We audited all interface surfaces in dark mode, curing contrast regressions across badge indicators, numeric counters, form inputs, call-to-action buttons, and calendar icons. Buttons such as the index CTA now boast high-contrast dark text on bright KLD Green, and secondary buttons feature clear luminous borders and crisp icons. Our automated Playwright suite confirmed 100% test success with zero regressions across both light and dark themes!
key_takeaways: Engineered dual-persona developer photography with light and dark portraits across all team touchpoints.
Created 300ms hardware-accelerated Cyber Glitch & RGB Split transition with instant preloading and Hover Peek preview.
Unified FAQ chatbot with the index 3D robot companion modal for a seamless multi-turn AI experience.
Hardened global dark mode styling, curing contrast anomalies across badges, counters, and action buttons.

title: Tactile De-Pilling, 14-Pillar Tech Architecture Overhaul, Filter Consolidation & 3D Typography Sharpness
summary_excerpt: Enforced strict paper aesthetic guidelines by eliminating decorative pill clutter across About Us and DevBlog, overhauled Technical Architecture to showcase our authentic 14-pillar stack (Three.js WebGL & GLTF robot, MySQL/MariaDB PDO, NVIDIA NIM AI), unified redundant reset controls, and eradicated 3D perspective blur for crystal-sharp typography.
full_story:
Today was a milestone in design purity, architectural transparency, and rendering precision. We eliminated decorative pill clutter, brought our technical documentation in line with our real 14-pillar engineering stack, unified student filter controls, and diagnosed and cured GPU texture magnification blur across our 3D stage.

As our project evolved, visual debt accumulated in the form of decorative rounded pill badges and stadium capsules that violated our tactile Paper Sheet aesthetic guidelines. I led a comprehensive cleanup across about-us.php, stripping away decorative eyebrow tags and transforming card badges, author date tags, developer role badges, and navigation controls into crisp, structured paper chips with subtle borders and intentional typography. In the interactive reader modal, I removed the redundant bottom close button and footer entirely, reclaiming prime reading space for engineering narratives and deliverables.

Overhauling Technical Architecture: The Authentic 14 Pillars

Our About Us page had previously displayed legacy placeholder notes referencing a flat-file JSON datastore. I completely replaced that section with an authentic 14-Pillar Technical Architecture Spec Grid (.tech-spec-grid). It transparently details our full production stack: Three.js WebGL & GLTFLoader driving our 3D robot mascot (cute_robot.glb) with 13 procedural kinematics and OLED visor shaders, MySQL 8.0/MariaDB (InnoDB) with ACID transactions, PHP PDO Prepared Statements with zero SQL injection vectors, atomic database migrations (database/migrate.php), Native PHP 8.2+ RBAC, NVIDIA NIM AI Gateway (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct) with multi-turn memory, local heuristic fallbacks, modular CSS design tokens, Bootstrap 5.3, vanilla ES6+ JavaScript with Shannon entropy calculations, 30s background notification polling, Bcrypt/anti-CSRF security, and our 26-spec Playwright E2E automation suite.

Student Jobs: Filter Consolidation & Category Data Integrity

On student/jobs.php, three competing reset controls previously crowded the viewport (hero banner reset pill, category header clear link, and toolbar reset button). I consolidated these down to a single authoritative reset button in the filter toolbar and replaced the hero pill with an informative Active Discipline badge. Concurrently, I tracked down an insidious category count bug in includes/data-helper.php where categories without active jobs retained static seed numbers; I fixed the aggregation fallback and seeded the missing Sports & Athletics Aide jobs (#9 and #10) so the live catalog perfectly matches database records.

Diagnosing & Eradicating 3D GPU Perspective Blur

When inspecting our 3D Coverflow DevBlog, we noticed a subtle rendering flaw: text on the front active card appeared fuzzy and blurry, while cards in the back remained sharp. Profiling Chromium's rendering pipeline revealed that translateZ(80px) under perspective: 1400px projected the front card 6% closer to the camera, forcing the GPU to stretch the 1x offscreen bitmap texture bilinearly instead of re-rasterizing vector glyphs. Meanwhile, back cards were scaled down (scale(0.86)), downsampling pixels crisply. Furthermore, transform-style: preserve-3d ignored DOM z-index, causing rotated side cards to slice through flat elements. I eliminated translateZ(80px), switched the track to transform-style: flat, and applied individual perspective to flanking cards. The active card now renders at exact 1:1 pixel scale with razor-sharp subpixel ClearType antialiasing and flawless z-index stacking!
key_takeaways: Enforced tactile paper design guidelines by de-pilling About Us and DevBlog, removing duplicate modal footer.
Overhauled Technical Architecture to showcase authentic 14-pillar stack featuring Three.js, MySQL PDO, and NVIDIA NIM.
Consolidated 3 redundant filter reset controls on student jobs and resolved category count aggregation bug.
Eliminated 3D GPU perspective texture magnification blur, restoring razor-sharp 1:1 subpixel typography on the active card.

title: Modular CSS Architecture, Role-Based Navbar, Multi-Turn AI Memory & 20-Hour Academic Labor Cap

full_story:

As systems grow in complexity, stylesheet maintenance can quickly degrade without strict discipline. I tackled this head-on today by breaking apart our monolithic custom.css into 7 domain-specific modules: variables.css, base.css, components.css, layout.css, auth.css, dashboard.css, and robot.css. To optimize asset delivery, I replaced timestamp query cache-busting with filemtime() in includes/header.php, ensuring optimal client caching while guaranteeing real-time updates when files are edited.

3-Column Role Navbar & Centered Spotlight Search

I completely restructured navbar.php using a clean 3-column CSS Grid. The campus brand logo now routes dynamically based on session role—sending students directly to student/dashboard.php, employers to their requisitions, and admins to analytical reports. For authenticated users, I introduced an elegant centered Google-style search bar that triggers our debounced universal spotlight search modal (Ctrl+K) without layout jitter or horizontal collisions.

Campus AI Multi-Turn Memory & Navigation Intelligence

I upgraded our Campus AI companion gateway by feeding the entire portal sitemap and session role context into the system prompt. Conversations now retain a sliding multi-turn conversational memory across faqs.php and the hero assistant, with plural-aware regex for our curated local offline fallback engine.

Institutional 20-Hour Labor Cap & Mobile Filters

To strictly adhere to the university standard safeguarding student academic standing, I implemented client and server-side validation capping weekly student assistant shifts to a hard maximum of 20 hours per week across job requisition creation and editing forms. Furthermore, I redesigned the shared footer into an unsegmented modern unit and transformed the mobile job search filters into a smooth collapsible accordion with live filter count badges.
key_takeaways: Modularized monolithic CSS into 7 scoped stylesheets and integrated filemtime() asset caching.
Engineered 3-column CSS Grid navbar with dynamic role-based logo routing and centered spotlight search.
Implemented multi-turn conversational memory and sitemap navigation in Campus AI companion.
Strictly enforced statutory 20-hour/week student labor cap with server-side validation.

title: Building the Multi-Role Notification Engine: Real-Time Polling, Verification Triggers & Migration Whitelists
summary_excerpt: Architected an asynchronous multi-role notification pipeline with 30-second background polling, lifecycle verification triggers across student applications and employer accreditations, and hardened database migration loops with strict table whitelisting.
full_story:
Clear communication and instantaneous feedback are critical for our multi-role institutional platform. Today, I built an end-to-end real-time in-app notification infrastructure.

I established the relational notifications table in MySQL with foreign key constraints, indexes, and automated cascading cleanup. In includes/data-helper.php, I implemented dynamic lifecycle event triggers: students receive instant updates when their application shifts state (Under Review, Interview Scheduled with date & venue, Accepted, Declined) and when profile change requests are resolved. Employers are alerted immediately upon new student submissions or when their institutional accreditation is verified, while admins receive real-time notifications for incoming registrations and student COR requests.

Navbar Dropdown, Toast Alerts & Notification Center

I engineered api/notifications.php and assets/js/notifications.js to handle 30-second background polling with document.visibilitychange lifecycle pausing to preserve battery and network bandwidth. Unread pings display non-intrusive floating toasts and increment the navbar bell counter. Furthermore, I built a dedicated Notification Center (notifications.php) featuring chip-filtered tabs (All/Unread), 'Mark All as Read', and direct deep-links to associated records.

Migration Truncate Whitelist Hardening

To eliminate any possibility of command injection or malicious table manipulation during database resets, I hardened database/migrate.php by wrapping all truncate operations in a strict table name whitelist array validated by regex prior to execution.
key_takeaways: Engineered relational notifications schema with user foreign keys and automated lifecycle triggers.
Built 30-second background polling engine with tab visibility suspension and floating toast alerts.
Developed comprehensive Notification Center (notifications.php) with unread filtering and batch actions.
Hardened database migration reset scripts with strict table whitelist and regex validation.

title: Giving Life to the Mascot: 13 Kinetic Animations, Typewriter Speech Bubble & Interactive Dialogue Modes
summary_excerpt: Elevated the 3D robot mascot with 13 expressive procedural animations, synchronized head and visor micro-motions, an interactive typewriter speech bubble, and dynamic dialogue modes (/boost, /grill-me, and Talk).
full_story:
Having established the 3D WebGL canvas yesterday, today's mission was giving our robot companion true personality, charisma, and emotional depth.

Every movement is smoothly interpolated through spring-damped matrices to prevent mechanical abruptness.

Interactive Speech Bubble & Typewriter Micro-Gestures

When students switch modes, the companion's OLED eye shader smoothly shifts colors—from KLD emerald green to alert amber and sharp cyan—providing immediate visual feedback.
key_takeaways: Programmed 13 procedural kinetic animations with spring damping and clamped kinematics.
Built dynamic typewriter speech bubble with synchronized mascot micro-gestures.
Implemented 3 interactive dialogue modes with real-time OLED emissive eye shader color transitions.
Optimized WebGL rendering loops with IntersectionObserver to conserve client device resources.

title: Relational Foreign Keys, Swarm Security Hardening & Permanent Demo/Real Data Coexistence
summary_excerpt: Implemented explicit MySQL foreign key constraints with EER semantic labels, conducted a comprehensive swarm security audit hardening MIME types and IDOR boundaries, and unified demo/real datastores for permanent coexistence.
full_story:
With MySQL fully active, today was dedicated to relational modeling rigor, database constraint enforcement, and ironclad defense-in-depth security.

I enhanced database/schema.sql with explicit semantic foreign key constraints (fk_jobs_category, fk_jobs_employer, fk_apps_job, fk_apps_student) and added UNIQUE KEY unique_student_job to prevent duplicate submissions at the relational level.

Swarm Security Audit & Defensive Hardening

I executed a comprehensive security audit across all entry points: whitelisted registration roles strictly to ['student', 'employer'] preventing privilege escalation to admin; upgraded authentication to native password_hash() and scrubbed hashes from session superglobals; implemented strict finfo_file MIME inspection on all document uploads; and scoped employer review endpoints strictly to primary-key ownership (employer_id === user['id']) to eradicate IDOR vulnerabilities.

Demo & Real Data Coexistence

I removed artificial dataset switching and destructive table wipes. Demo benchmark listings and live registered student/employer accounts now coexist permanently in MySQL, with live admin COR/ID verification inspection modals in admin/users.php that sync immediately to active sessions.
key_takeaways: Defined explicit relational foreign key constraints and UNIQUE (job_id, student_id) indexes.
Hardened authentication, file upload MIME validation, anti-CSRF tokens, and security headers.
Enforced strict IDOR primary-key ownership checks across employer review endpoints.
Enabled permanent coexistence of demo fixtures and real registered user records.

title: Enterprise MySQL Migration: Relational Schema, ACID Migrations & Full-Width 100vh Hero Viewport
summary_excerpt: Migrated the entire data persistence architecture from flat-file JSON to MySQL (PDO) with ACID migrations, expanded the viewport to 100% full-width with a 100vh landing hero, and verified all 106 Playwright tests.
full_story:
Flat-file JSON persistence carried our prototype through early milestones, but enterprise scalability and concurrent applicant handling demanded a true relational database.

Today marked our largest architectural leap: migrating the data layer to MySQL/MariaDB via PHP Data Objects (PDO). I established includes/db.php as a secure PDO connection singleton and performed a complete rewrite of includes/data-helper.php. Every read, write, filter, and state transition now executes via parameterized SQL queries, completely eliminating SQL injection risks and multi-process file concurrency race conditions.

ACID Database Migration & Seeding Engine

I built database/schema.sql and database/migrate.php, creating an automated CLI and browser migration runner. The engine wraps schema initialization, table truncations, and JSON seed data re-import into a single atomic ACID transaction, enabling instantaneous database resets without schema corruption.

100vh Hero Section & Full-Width Paper Sheet

I expanded the portal canvas by removing artificial max-width constraints on .sheet for a 100% full-width layout. I constructed an expansive 100vh full-screen landing hero section with vertically centered typography, elevated partner strips, and split student registration name fields (First, Middle, Last). Ran our entire automated Playwright test suite—achieving 106/106 passed tests with zero regressions!
key_takeaways: Replaced flat-file JSON storage with enterprise MySQL (PDO) prepared statements across all queries.
Engineered transactional CLI/web database migration engine (database/migrate.php).
Expanded portal layout to full-width with an immersive 100vh hero viewport and split name fields.
Achieved 100% pass rate across 106 automated Playwright E2E test specs on the new relational engine.

title: The Start of the Madness: All-Day Coding Sprint & 1:00 AM Optimization Marathon
summary_excerpt: Pushed through an intensive full-day coding marathon from early morning to 1:00 AM—building the zero-DB JSON persistence engine, session state synchronization, password entropy meter, and end-to-end application workflows.
full_story:
August 27 was the true start of creating this madness. The moment I woke up in the morning, I jumped directly into the codebase to develop and optimize the core architecture even further.

For the entire day, I worked non-stop on our zero-database data architecture. I built includes/data-helper.php, establishing atomic file reads/writes for our JSON datasets and synchronizing live states into $_SESSION for zero database overhead and lightning-fast responses.

Security Algorithms & Shift Availability Matrix

I engineered the standalone client-side Shannon password entropy analyzer (password-strength.js) with real-time criteria checkmarks, role-based access control (RBAC), and built the interactive 18-slot weekly schedule availability time grid matrix for student job submissions.

Pushing Through to 1:00 AM

I coded and optimized straight through the evening and night, finally stopping at 1:00 AM on August 28, hoping that this intensive development foundation would be solid and comprehensive enough for our project.
key_takeaways: Engineered zero-database atomic JSON persistence and dynamic session synchronization.
Implemented real-time client-side password entropy scoring and visual strength feedback.
Built the 18-slot weekly schedule availability grid matrix for student applications.
Completed a grueling 16+ hour coding marathon ending at 1:00 AM for core engine stability.

title: Genesis of the System: Topic Selection, Architecture Drafting & Pure PHP Foundations
summary_excerpt: Kicked off on topic selection day—immediately drafted the architecture, cataloged requirements, explored UI inspirations, and began non-stop coding during every free hour adhering strictly to pure PHP with zero static HTML.
full_story:
Our journey began on August 26, 2026—the day our team picked the project topic for our COAL101 Web Systems and Technologies midterm lab project.

As soon as we chose the Campus Job Posting System, we didn't waste a single moment. We planned immediately, structured the project directory hierarchy, listed every functional module we would need, and researched modern design inspirations suited for a premier institutional portal.

Strict Stack Compliance: Native PHP, No Raw HTML

During our free time that day on campus, we started drafting the site. We strictly limited our stack to what our professor permitted: Native PHP, CSS, Bootstrap 5.3, and Vanilla JavaScript—with strictly no standalone HTML files as our professor instructed. Every page had to be dynamically composed via modular PHP components.

Lead Developer Dedication

As the lead of this development, I simply couldn't stop thinking about the system. I continued developing through another free period that same day and kept writing code up until we went home, determined to finish the foundational task.
key_takeaways: Selected the Campus Job Posting System topic and mapped all functional requirements.
Enforced pure Native PHP modular template architecture with zero static .html files.
Defined initial JSON datastore schemas for users, categories, jobs, and applications.
Developed continuously through campus free periods and after going home to build the skeleton.
